info.summary: DAPPER scientific content, knowledge-gap search, and shared analysis/paragraph jobs.
info.description: Local API implementation contract; production deployment is deferred. Scientific schemas are generated from the pinned DAPPER schema. Application envelopes handle ownership, drafts, search, jobs and pagination. All DAPPER IDs in scientific examples are computed, not placeholders. Research/job/user timestamps and semantic rankings are illustrative; no Claude Code or embedding run was performed. The account fixture is the approved 12-claim HTML example: captured CFDE observations plus explicitly invented KG/membership assertions, never a production grounding-pass example. The evidence package is a separately verified live capture, not a claim that this example account was generated from it. Examples using example.org are not live resources. Do not treat example output as published research.

knowledge_gaps.text: Are the CAD PGS×context interactions driven by adverse exposures causally amplifying genetic risk, or are some "contexts" actually downstream readouts of incipient disease (reverse causation)?
knowledge_gaps.gap_description: Population PGS×context analyses (Nagpal & Gibson 2026, PMID:42443528) are largely unable to establish the causality of specific contexts. dismech separates true environmental exposures (smoking, high-fat diet, sedentary lifestyle) from biochemical readouts (LDL, HDL, C-reactive protein); the biochemical "contexts" are prime reverse-causation suspects, since they may be partly downstream of the atherosclerotic process rather than upstream drivers, and behavioural contexts such as reduced physical activity may be rapid responses to incipient angina rather than causes. Distinguishing genuine amplification of genetic effects from reverse causation determines whether the modelled interventions (e.g. lowering cholesterol in high-PGS smokers) would actually reduce risk.

proposed_experiments.name: Mendelian randomization of exposure-to-CAD direction across PGS strata
proposed_experiments.description: Use bidirectional / multivariable Mendelian randomization to test whether each candidate context (LDL, HDL, C-reactive protein, smoking) causally affects CAD versus being a consequence of subclinical disease, and whether the causal effect estimate scales with polygenic liability as the amplification model predicts.
proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: A context is retained as a causal amplifier if MR supports exposure-to-disease directionality and the exposure-attributable risk difference increases across increasing PGS strata; it is flagged as a reverse-causation suspect otherwise.

proposed_experiments.name: Prospective incident-CAD analysis restricted to pre-diagnosis exposure windows
proposed_experiments.description: Restrict exposures to measurements taken well before diagnosis and repeat the PGS×context liability-threshold modelling on incident cases only, to reduce the chance that exposure values reflect behavioural responses to early disease.
proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: Amplification is supported if the PGS×context deviation from additivity persists when only pre-diagnosis exposure windows and incident cases are used.

get.description: Browse imported DisMech gaps ordered by distinct scientific-account count descending. Public scope (default) counts only explicitly published snapshots across users; workspace scope requires a session and counts owned saved accounts. Equal-count gaps shuffle on each new browse; a server seed in the signed continuation cursor preserves tie order across pages. Exact gap digests only: no text matching, attempts, paragraph jobs or implicit source-revision rollup. Invalid supplied credentials are rejected even for public reads. Filters apply before pagination; count or corpus changes expire cursors. sort=votes orders by net gap vote score, then account count, then the same seeded tie order. sort=accounts is the default. Vote changes, sort changes and registered-viewer changes expire cursors. Account votes do not contribute to gap vote totals. Counts include current accounts only: accounts archived by a reference reload stay listed but are not counted.

The cited disturbed-flow evidence derives from mouse carotid arteries and human carotid plaques, so its transfer to coronary endothelial dysfunction is explicitly partial.

post.summary: Start an analysis or paragraph job
post.description: Replaces analysis-runs and account-specific paragraph-run creation. kind=analysis freezes draft/version, creates a research request and enqueues atomically. kind=paragraph uses an already saved account. Trusted backend supplies attribution, model/harness configuration and dates. Paid execution is asynchronous; 202 does not imply a successful scientific result. Idempotent replay returns the original job and never starts another paid attempt. Analysis submission requires an exact imported DisMech gap and nonempty resolved CFDE anchors. Freeze the saved source/mapping-run bindings and native IDs with the request; later mapping imports do not retarget historical jobs. Label/gene disagreement does not reject a mapped anchor. Persist each accepted account with an outbox record that automatically schedules its default paragraph job, unique by account payload, citation pins and paragraph settings. Analysis completion does not wait for paragraph success. Manual paragraph jobs support retries or alternate focus/settings. Analysis anchors must belong to the active reference generation (409 REFERENCE_GENERATION_SUPERSEDED: start a new analysis on the gap with current factors), and analysis submission waits while a reference reload is in progress (503 REFERENCE_RELOAD_IN_PROGRESS). Paragraph jobs, including on archived accounts, are not affected.

knowledge_gaps.text: Are the CAD PGS×context interactions driven by adverse exposures causally amplifying genetic risk, or are some "contexts" actually downstream readouts of incipient disease (reverse causation)?
knowledge_gaps.gap_description: Population PGS×context analyses (Nagpal & Gibson 2026, PMID:42443528) are largely unable to establish the causality of specific contexts. dismech separates true environmental exposures (smoking, high-fat diet, sedentary lifestyle) from biochemical readouts (LDL, HDL, C-reactive protein); the biochemical "contexts" are prime reverse-causation suspects, since they may be partly downstream of the atherosclerotic process rather than upstream drivers, and behavioural contexts such as reduced physical activity may be rapid responses to incipient angina rather than causes. Distinguishing genuine amplification of genetic effects from reverse causation determines whether the modelled interventions (e.g. lowering cholesterol in high-PGS smokers) would actually reduce risk.

scientific_accounts.name: Genes and gene programs in a shared CAD-in-T2D mechanism
scientific_accounts.question: dapper:KnowledgeGap.zNV20nhHamt-a4CeAktQQPoAivOJe6xk
scientific_accounts.context: A CAD-in-T2D evidence slice used to investigate the selected broader CAD gap. This authored design packet combines captured CFDE observations with explicitly illustrative KG membership assertions. No live agent ran.
scientific_accounts.closing_remarks: SHH, GLI3 and TCF7L2, together with the AMP AD / GTEx and PsychENCODE geneM16 programs, are implicated in the same CAD-in-T2D mechanism by their captured EAGGL loadings. Their PIGEAN trait-level results connect these assessments to CAD in people with type 2 diabetes. The illustrative membership assertions show how genes could be connected to the programs, but those links remain unverified. Together, the assessed relationships prioritize a mechanism for investigating the selected gap. They do not distinguish exposure-driven amplification of genetic risk from downstream readouts or reverse causation; that requires temporal or intervention evidence not present here.

knowledge_gaps.text: Are the CAD PGS×context interactions driven by adverse exposures causally amplifying genetic risk, or are some "contexts" actually downstream readouts of incipient disease (reverse causation)?
knowledge_gaps.gap_description: Population PGS×context analyses (Nagpal & Gibson 2026, PMID:42443528) are largely unable to establish the causality of specific contexts. dismech separates true environmental exposures (smoking, high-fat diet, sedentary lifestyle) from biochemical readouts (LDL, HDL, C-reactive protein); the biochemical "contexts" are prime reverse-causation suspects, since they may be partly downstream of the atherosclerotic process rather than upstream drivers, and behavioural contexts such as reduced physical activity may be rapid responses to incipient angina rather than causes. Distinguishing genuine amplification of genetic effects from reverse causation determines whether the modelled interventions (e.g. lowering cholesterol in high-PGS smokers) would actually reduce risk.

scientific_accounts.name: Genes and gene programs in a shared CAD-in-T2D mechanism
scientific_accounts.question: dapper:KnowledgeGap.zNV20nhHamt-a4CeAktQQPoAivOJe6xk
scientific_accounts.context: A CAD-in-T2D evidence slice used to investigate the selected broader CAD gap. This authored design packet combines captured CFDE observations with explicitly illustrative KG membership assertions. No live agent ran.
scientific_accounts.closing_remarks: SHH, GLI3 and TCF7L2, together with the AMP AD / GTEx and PsychENCODE geneM16 programs, are implicated in the same CAD-in-T2D mechanism by their captured EAGGL loadings. Their PIGEAN trait-level results connect these assessments to CAD in people with type 2 diabetes. The illustrative membership assertions show how genes could be connected to the programs, but those links remain unverified. Together, the assessed relationships prioritize a mechanism for investigating the selected gap. They do not distinguish exposure-driven amplification of genetic risk from downstream readouts or reverse causation; that requires temporal or intervention evidence not present here.

scientific_accounts.closing_remarks: SHH, GLI3 and TCF7L2, together with the AMP AD / GTEx and PsychENCODE geneM16 programs, are implicated in the same CAD-in-T2D mechanism by their captured EAGGL loadings. Their PIGEAN trait-level results connect these assessments to CAD in people with type 2 diabetes. The illustrative membership assertions show how genes could be connected to the programs, but those links remain unverified. Together, the assessed relationships prioritize a mechanism for investigating the selected gap. They do not distinguish exposure-driven amplification of genetic risk from downstream readouts or reverse causation; that requires temporal or intervention evidence not present here.

knowledge_gaps.text: Are the CAD PGS×context interactions driven by adverse exposures causally amplifying genetic risk, or are some "contexts" actually downstream readouts of incipient disease (reverse causation)?
knowledge_gaps.gap_description: Population PGS×context analyses (Nagpal & Gibson 2026, PMID:42443528) are largely unable to establish the causality of specific contexts. dismech separates true environmental exposures (smoking, high-fat diet, sedentary lifestyle) from biochemical readouts (LDL, HDL, C-reactive protein); the biochemical "contexts" are prime reverse-causation suspects, since they may be partly downstream of the atherosclerotic process rather than upstream drivers, and behavioural contexts such as reduced physical activity may be rapid responses to incipient angina rather than causes. Distinguishing genuine amplification of genetic effects from reverse causation determines whether the modelled interventions (e.g. lowering cholesterol in high-PGS smokers) would actually reduce risk.

paragraphs.text: The selected CAD knowledge gap asks whether context amplifies genetic risk or instead reflects incipient disease. In the captured CAD-in-T2D analysis, SHH, GLI3 and TCF7L2 are implicated in mechanism Factor1 by EAGGL loadings of 0.5042, 0.3245 and 0.3813, respectively. The AMP AD / GTEx brain-aging and PsychENCODE geneM16 programs are also implicated in this mechanism by their gene-set loadings. PIGEAN gene–trait and gene-set–trait results further connect these genes and programs to CAD in people with type 2 diabetes. Illustrative, unverified KG membership assertions connect SHH to the AMP AD / GTEx set and TCF7L2 to the PsychENCODE set; these links demonstrate a possible evidence connection and are not retrieved biological findings. Taken together, these assessments prioritize a shared mechanism for investigating the gap, but do not resolve whether exposures amplify genetic risk or are downstream readouts. Temporal or intervention evidence is still needed.

knowledge_gaps.text: Are the CAD PGS×context interactions driven by adverse exposures causally amplifying genetic risk, or are some "contexts" actually downstream readouts of incipient disease (reverse causation)?
knowledge_gaps.gap_description: Population PGS×context analyses (Nagpal & Gibson 2026, PMID:42443528) are largely unable to establish the causality of specific contexts. dismech separates true environmental exposures (smoking, high-fat diet, sedentary lifestyle) from biochemical readouts (LDL, HDL, C-reactive protein); the biochemical "contexts" are prime reverse-causation suspects, since they may be partly downstream of the atherosclerotic process rather than upstream drivers, and behavioural contexts such as reduced physical activity may be rapid responses to incipient angina rather than causes. Distinguishing genuine amplification of genetic effects from reverse causation determines whether the modelled interventions (e.g. lowering cholesterol in high-PGS smokers) would actually reduce risk.

account.question: dapper:KnowledgeGap.zNV20nhHamt-a4CeAktQQPoAivOJe6xk
account.context: A CAD-in-T2D evidence slice used to investigate the selected broader CAD gap. This authored design packet combines captured CFDE observations with explicitly illustrative KG membership assertions. No live agent ran.
account.closing_remarks: SHH, GLI3 and TCF7L2, together with the AMP AD / GTEx and PsychENCODE geneM16 programs, are implicated in the same CAD-in-T2D mechanism by their captured EAGGL loadings. Their PIGEAN trait-level results connect these assessments to CAD in people with type 2 diabetes. The illustrative membership assertions show how genes could be connected to the programs, but those links remain unverified. Together, the assessed relationships prioritize a mechanism for investigating the selected gap. They do not distinguish exposure-driven amplification of genetic risk from downstream readouts or reverse causation; that requires temporal or intervention evidence not present here.

Distinguishing genuine amplification of genetic effects from reverse causation determines whether the modelled interventions (e.g. lowering cholesterol in high-PGS smokers) would actually reduce risk.

account.name: Genes and gene programs in a shared CAD-in-T2D mechanism
account.question: dapper:KnowledgeGap.zNV20nhHamt-a4CeAktQQPoAivOJe6xk
account.context: A CAD-in-T2D evidence slice used to investigate the selected broader CAD gap. This authored design packet combines captured CFDE observations with explicitly illustrative KG membership assertions. No live agent ran.
account.closing_remarks: SHH, GLI3 and TCF7L2, together with the AMP AD / GTEx and PsychENCODE geneM16 programs, are implicated in the same CAD-in-T2D mechanism by their captured EAGGL loadings. Their PIGEAN trait-level results connect these assessments to CAD in people with type 2 diabetes. The illustrative membership assertions show how genes could be connected to the programs, but those links remain unverified. Together, the assessed relationships prioritize a mechanism for investigating the selected gap. They do not distinguish exposure-driven amplification of genetic risk from downstream readouts or reverse causation; that requires temporal or intervention evidence not present here.

knowledge_gap.text: Are the CAD PGS×context interactions driven by adverse exposures causally amplifying genetic risk, or are some "contexts" actually downstream readouts of incipient disease (reverse causation)?
knowledge_gap.gap_description: Population PGS×context analyses (Nagpal & Gibson 2026, PMID:42443528) are largely unable to establish the causality of specific contexts. dismech separates true environmental exposures (smoking, high-fat diet, sedentary lifestyle) from biochemical readouts (LDL, HDL, C-reactive protein); the biochemical "contexts" are prime reverse-causation suspects, since they may be partly downstream of the atherosclerotic process rather than upstream drivers, and behavioural contexts such as reduced physical activity may be rapid responses to incipient angina rather than causes. Distinguishing genuine amplification of genetic effects from reverse causation determines whether the modelled interventions (e.g. lowering cholesterol in high-PGS smokers) would actually reduce risk.

knowledge_gap.gap_description: Population PGS×context analyses (Nagpal & Gibson 2026, PMID:42443528) are largely unable to establish the causality of specific contexts. dismech separates true environmental exposures (smoking, high-fat diet, sedentary lifestyle) from biochemical readouts (LDL, HDL, C-reactive protein); the biochemical "contexts" are prime reverse-causation suspects, since they may be partly downstream of the atherosclerotic process rather than upstream drivers, and behavioural contexts such as reduced physical activity may be rapid responses to incipient angina rather than causes. Distinguishing genuine amplification of genetic effects from reverse causation determines whether the modelled interventions (e.g. lowering cholesterol in high-PGS smokers) would actually reduce risk.

proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: A context is retained as a causal amplifier if MR supports exposure-to-disease directionality and the exposure-attributable risk difference increases across increasing PGS strata; it is flagged as a reverse-causation suspect otherwise.
proposed_experiments.description: Use bidirectional / multivariable Mendelian randomization to test whether each candidate context (LDL, HDL, C-reactive protein, smoking) causally affects CAD versus being a consequence of subclinical disease, and whether the causal effect estimate scales with polygenic liability as the amplification model predicts.
proposed_experiments.name: Mendelian randomization of exposure-to-CAD direction across PGS strata

proposed_experiments.decision_criterion: Amplification is supported if the PGS×context deviation from additivity persists when only pre-diagnosis exposure windows and incident cases are used.
proposed_experiments.description: Restrict exposures to measurements taken well before diagnosis and repeat the PGS×context liability-threshold modelling on incident cases only, to reduce the chance that exposure values reflect behavioural responses to early disease.
proposed_experiments.name: Prospective incident-CAD analysis restricted to pre-diagnosis exposure windows

dismech:disorders/Coronary_Artery_Diseas.description: At atherosclerosis-prone arterial sites, disturbed flow is associated with endothelial stress and senescence, while reduced endothelial nitric-oxide biosynthesis represents the vasomotor dysfunction that impairs dilation. This nonconforming coronary endothelial-function branch is modeled separately from the conserved subendothelial apoB-retention trigger. The cited disturbed-flow evidence derives from mouse carotid arteries and human carotid plaques, so its transfer to coronary endothelial dysfunction is explicitly partial.

downstream.description: Connects the vasomotor and disturbed-flow endothelial branch to the conserved retention trigger without asserting that reduced nitric oxide alone is sufficient for apoB retention.

evidence.explanation: Links arterial injury and endothelial dysfunction to subendothelial apoB modification and monocyte entry, but does not isolate nitric-oxide loss or directly establish every intermediate in lipoprotein retention.
evidence.reference_title: The Role of Lipids and Lipoproteins in Atherosclerosis.
evidence.snippet: Arterial injury causes endothelial dysfunction promoting modification of apoB containing lipoproteins and infiltration of monocytes into the subendothelial space.

intermediate_mechanisms: increased endothelial permeability and apoB-lipoprotein entry
downstream.target: Coronary Endothelial Injury and Subendothelial LDL Retention

evidence.explanation: Supports disturbed-flow-associated endothelial senescence as one component of endothelial dysfunction. It does not directly measure nitric-oxide biosynthesis and comes from a mouse carotid model, so it is not treated as direct coronary or nitric-oxide evidence.
evidence.reference_title: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis of mouse carotid artery under disturbed flow and human carotid plaques identifies key cell populations in atherosclerosis development.
evidence.snippet: CD36 + positive ECs exhibited significant senescence phenotypes following disturbed flow stimulation.

evidence.explanation: Supports disturbed flow as a regional context for atherosclerosis and endothelial dysfunction. It does not directly establish reduced nitric-oxide biosynthesis or a coronary-specific effect.
evidence.reference_title: Single-cell RNA-seq analysis of mouse carotid artery under disturbed flow and human carotid plaques identifies key cell populations in atherosclerosis development.
evidence.snippet: Atherosclerosis tends to occur in regions of disturbed blood flow. This study explored how disturbed flow aggravates atherosclerosis using single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) datasets from mouse carotid arteries under disturbed flow and human carotid artery plaques.

evidence.explanation: EAS consensus statement concludes that LDL is causal for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, supporting elevated LDL cholesterol as a major risk factor for coronary plaque formation.
evidence.reference_title: Low-density lipoproteins cause atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. 1. Evidence from genetic, epidemiologic, and clinical studies. A consensus statement from the European Atherosclerosis Society Consensus Panel.
evidence.snippet: Consistent evidence from numerous and multiple different types of clinical and genetic studies unequivocally establishes that LDL causes ASCVD.

record.name: LDL Cholesterol

readouts.description: Circulating LDL cholesterol indexes the pool of apoB-containing lipoprotein available for retention in the coronary subendothelial space, so its level reports on the intensity of the retention step rather than being caused by it.
readouts.target: Coronary Endothelial Injury and Subendothelial LDL Retention

evidence.explanation: Individual-participant meta-analysis quantifies the association between circulating C-reactive protein and incident coronary heart disease, supporting CRP as an inflammatory risk marker in coronary artery disease.
evidence.reference_title: C-reactive protein concentration and risk of coronary heart disease, stroke, and mortality: an individual participant meta-analysis.
evidence.snippet: Risk ratios (RRs) for coronary heart disease per 1-SD higher log(e) CRP concentration (three-fold higher) were 1.63 (95% CI 1.51-1.76) when initially adjusted for age and sex only, and 1.37 (1.27-1.48) when adjusted further for conventional risk factors

readouts.description: C-reactive protein is a systemic acute-phase index that rises with the inflammatory activity of which intimal monocyte recruitment and foam-cell formation are part. It is a correlate of that intimal process and of coronary risk, not a direct measurement of the lesion.
readouts.target: Monocyte Recruitment and Macrophage Foam Cell Formation

evidence.explanation: INTERHEART, a standardised case-control study of acute myocardial infarction across 52 countries with 15152 cases and 14820 controls. Establishes smoking as one of the largest modifiable contributors to population attributable risk.

evidence.snippet: Smoking (odds ratio 2.87 for current vs never, PAR 35.7% for current and former vs never)

evidence.explanation: The tobacco-specific INTERHEART analysis. Quoted for the dose-response relationship, which is the part of the note the odds ratio alone does not establish.

evidence.snippet: risk increased by 5.6% for every additional cigarette smoked

value.plain_text:
Genes and gene programs in a shared CAD-in-T2D mechanism

The selected CAD knowledge gap asks whether context amplifies genetic risk or instead reflects incipient disease. [1] In the captured CAD-in-T2D analysis, SHH, GLI3 and TCF7L2 are implicated in mechanism Factor1 by EAGGL loadings of 0.5042, 0.3245 and 0.3813, respectively. [2, 3, 4] The AMP AD / GTEx brain-aging and PsychENCODE geneM16 programs are also implicated in this mechanism by their gene-set loadings. [5, 6] PIGEAN gene–trait and gene-set–trait results further connect these genes and programs to CAD in people with type 2 diabetes. [7, 8, 9, 10, 11] Illustrative, unverified KG membership assertions connect SHH to the AMP AD / GTEx set and TCF7L2 to the PsychENCODE set; these links demonstrate a possible evidence connection and are not retrieved biological findings. [12, 13] Taken together, these assessments prioritize a shared mechanism for investigating the gap, but do not resolve whether exposures amplify genetic risk or are downstream readouts. Temporal or intervention evidence is still needed. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]

DapperAgenticWorkspace.description:
A workspace in which an AI agent can re-run an Activity, plus the prompt that asks it to. This is the agentic counterpart of the executable provenance an Activity already carries: `command` and `container_image` tell a machine how to replay a step, while `regeneration_prompt` and `workspace_url` tell an agent how to.
It is typed `prov:Plan` because that is what it is in PROV terms — a description of intended execution, not the execution itself. The run remains the Activity; this is the recipe the agent follows. Keeping them separate matters: re-running a plan produces a NEW Activity, and conflating the two would make a regenerated result indistinguishable from the original.
WARNING ON REPRODUCIBILITY. A prompt is not a deterministic replay mechanism. The same prompt, workspace, and model can yield a different result run to run. Treat `regeneration_prompt` as documentation of intent that a human or agent can act on, NOT as a guarantee of bit-identical output — that is what `command` plus `container_image` plus `code_version` are for. Record the model and version actually used so a divergent re-run can at least be explained.

agent_model.description: Model that ran, or is expected to run, the prompt (e.g. "claude-fable-5"). Recorded so a divergent re-run can be explained.

agent_role.description: The software agent acting in this workspace — an npx:SoftwareAgent, which is also how a nanopublication attributes an assertion to a non-human author.

regeneration_prompt.description: The prompt that asks an agent to regenerate this analysis. Write it self-contained: an agent opening the workspace cold should be able to act on it without the surrounding conversation.

workspace_key.description: The hosting platform's own identifier for the workspace, when it differs from this node's `id` — for an akleao fork, the slug in its URL.

workspace_url.description: Resolvable URL for the workspace — where a person or agent goes to open it. In the example of akleao this is a fork URL, `https://www.akleao.com/fork/<slug-id>`: one shareable link that opens the workspace, rather than a path through project and branch ids. Required in spirit: a workspace nobody can reach is not provenance, it is a note.

DapperCellState.description: A cellular phenotype defined by the combination of GenePrograms active in a cell (or cell population) — e.g. "activated", "exhausted", "hypoxic". Distinct from a cell TYPE (a Cell Ontology class, e.g. `obo:CL_0000542`): a CellState is a functional/transcriptional state a cell of a given type can transition into and out of, defined by which programs are switched on — not which lineage the cell belongs to. No ontology term is asserted as class_uri — no term resolving to "cell state" as a generic, cross-cell-type phenotype was found (verified against EBI OLS4) — so CellState grounds via `is_a: HashableNode` directly. Mixes in `ProvenancedResource` so a CellState is citable and attributable the same way a `GeneProgram` (via `Set`) already is.

DapperGeneProgram.description: A Set whose members are genes that co-vary as a coordinated unit and together carry out a biological process — a factor from matrix factorization (cNMF, NMF, Spectra, WGCNA) or a curated gene module. No ontology term is asserted as class_uri — none resolves to "gene program" / "gene expression program" (verified against EBI OLS4) — so GeneProgram grounds via `is_a: Set` (prov:Collection), the same way GeneSet does. Distinct from GeneSet: a GeneSet is typically a static annotation (e.g. an MSigDB term); a GeneProgram is inferred from expression covariance and is usually a quantitative loading over genes, not just membership. `member_weights`, when present, is that loading — one number per gene in `members`, positionally paired. A very large loading matrix should still reference its source file via the member-manifest escape hatch `Set` already provides rather than enumerate weights here.

DapperHashableNode.description:
A Node whose `id` is a computed content address of the form `dapper:{ClassName}.{digest}` — the full LinkML class name, a dot, then a GA4GH `sha512t24u` digest over the slots marked `hashable`.
The digest covers hashable slots ONLY. Timestamps, signatures, mirror observations, workspace locations, and back-references are marked `unhashable` so that re-running, re-signing, mirroring, or re-hosting an artifact never changes what it is. See schema/identity/README.md for the DAPPER-ID-1 profile and schema/trusty-identifiers.md for why this is deliberately NOT a Trusty URI `RA` code.

PackageAgenticWorkspace.description:
A workspace in which an AI agent can re-run an Activity, plus the prompt that asks it to. This is the agentic counterpart of the executable provenance an Activity already carries: `command` and `container_image` tell a machine how to replay a step, while `regeneration_prompt` and `workspace_url` tell an agent how to.
It is typed `prov:Plan` because that is what it is in PROV terms — a description of intended execution, not the execution itself. The run remains the Activity; this is the recipe the agent follows. Keeping them separate matters: re-running a plan produces a NEW Activity, and conflating the two would make a regenerated result indistinguishable from the original.
WARNING ON REPRODUCIBILITY. A prompt is not a deterministic replay mechanism. The same prompt, workspace, and model can yield a different result run to run. Treat `regeneration_prompt` as documentation of intent that a human or agent can act on, NOT as a guarantee of bit-identical output — that is what `command` plus `container_image` plus `code_version` are for. Record the model and version actually used so a divergent re-run can at least be explained.

agent_model.description: Model that ran, or is expected to run, the prompt (e.g. "claude-fable-5"). Recorded so a divergent re-run can be explained.

agent_role.description: The software agent acting in this workspace — an npx:SoftwareAgent, which is also how a nanopublication attributes an assertion to a non-human author.

id.description: Unique identifier for a node — a CURIE shorthand or a full URI. For a Dataset this is its persistent identifier (e.g. a DOI).

last_run.description: When the prompt was last executed in this workspace.

platform.description: The system hosting the workspace, e.g. "akleao", "Claude Code".

regeneration_prompt.description: The prompt that asks an agent to regenerate this analysis. Write it self-contained: an agent opening the workspace cold should be able to act on it without the surrounding conversation.

workspace_key.description: The hosting platform's own identifier for the workspace, when it differs from this node's `id` — for an akleao fork, the slug in its URL.

workspace_url.description: Resolvable URL for the workspace — where a person or agent goes to open it. In the example of akleao this is a fork URL, `https://www.akleao.com/fork/<slug-id>`: one shareable link that opens the workspace, rather than a path through project and branch ids. Required in spirit: a workspace nobody can reach is not provenance, it is a note.

PackageCellState.description: A cellular phenotype defined by the combination of GenePrograms active in a cell (or cell population) — e.g. "activated", "exhausted", "hypoxic". Distinct from a cell TYPE (a Cell Ontology class, e.g. `obo:CL_0000542`): a CellState is a functional/transcriptional state a cell of a given type can transition into and out of, defined by which programs are switched on — not which lineage the cell belongs to. No ontology term is asserted as class_uri — no term resolving to "cell state" as a generic, cross-cell-type phenotype was found (verified against EBI OLS4) — so CellState grounds via `is_a: HashableNode` directly. Mixes in `ProvenancedResource` so a CellState is citable and attributable the same way a `GeneProgram` (via `Set`) already is.

A DOI answers "what does the publisher call this, and how do I cite it?". Both are worth keeping, so neither displaces the other. `identifier_type` names the scheme.

PackageDrsObject.description: GA4GH DRS object identity for a dataset file/object. PackageGeneProgram.description: A Set whose members are genes that co-vary as a coordinated unit and together carry out a biological process — a factor from matrix factorization (cNMF, NMF, Spectra, WGCNA) or a curated gene module. No ontology term is asserted as class_uri — none resolves to "gene program" / "gene expression program" (verified against EBI OLS4) — so GeneProgram grounds via `is_a: Set` (prov:Collection), the same way GeneSet does. Distinct from GeneSet: a GeneSet is typically a static annotation (e.g. an MSigDB term); a GeneProgram is inferred from expression covariance and is usually a quantitative loading over genes, not just membership. `member_weights`, when present, is that loading — one number per gene in `members`, positionally paired. A very large loading matrix should still reference its source file via the member-manifest escape hatch `Set` already provides rather than enumerate weights here.

alternate_identifier.description: Externally-assigned persistent identifiers for this resource — a DOI, an accession, a Handle, an ARK. `id` is DAPPER's own computed content address (`dapper:{ClassName}.{digest}`), which answers "what exactly is this record?". A DOI answers "what does the publisher call this, and how do I cite it?". Both are worth keeping, so neither displaces the other. `identifier_type` names the scheme.

Not necessarily raw expression: it is whatever per-gene number the `inference_method` produces. Reordering or resizing one list without the other breaks the pairing.

validity_score.description: Is the output real biology? Evidence from hallmark pathway enrichment, GWAS genetic signals, and cell-surface markers. Weighted 50% into `quality_score`.

PackageHashableNode.description:
A Node whose `id` is a computed content address of the form `dapper:{ClassName}.{digest}` — the full LinkML class name, a dot, then a GA4GH `sha512t24u` digest over the slots marked `hashable`.
The digest covers hashable slots ONLY. Timestamps, signatures, mirror observations, workspace locations, and back-references are marked `unhashable` so that re-running, re-signing, mirroring, or re-hosting an artifact never changes what it is. See schema/identity/README.md for the DAPPER-ID-1 profile and schema/trusty-identifiers.md for why this is deliberately NOT a Trusty URI `RA` code.

PackageNanopublication.description: A nanopublication: an assertion plus its provenance plus its publication info, published as one signed, content-addressed unit. All THREE of `has_assertion`, `has_provenance` and `has_publication_info` are required — the well-formedness rules demand exactly one quad for each, so a nanopub with only an assertion is malformed and the network will reject it. `id` is the nanopub's trusty URI once published (a draft may use a temporary URI).

created_from_template.description: The Nanodash template this nanopub was instantiated from. Knowledge Pixels tooling emits this alongside `ntemplate:wasCreatedFromProvenanceTemplate` and `...FromPubinfoTemplate`.

has_assertion.description: The assertion graph. REQUIRED: nanopublication well-formedness demands exactly one `np:hasAssertion` quad in the Head.

has_provenance.description: The provenance graph — where the ASSERTION came from (not where the nanopub came from; that is pubinfo). REQUIRED: exactly one, same as the assertion. A nanopub carrying only an assertion is malformed.

has_publication_info.description: The publication-info graph — where the NANOPUB itself came from. REQUIRED: exactly one.

id.description: Unique identifier for a node — a CURIE shorthand or a full URI. For a Dataset this is its persistent identifier (e.g. a DOI).

invalidates.description: Nanopublication(s) this one invalidates without formally superseding them.

nanopub_license.description: License CURIE/URI the nanopublication is released under.

supersedes.description: A previously published nanopub this one replaces. Because trusty URIs are immutable, this — not editing — is how a nanopub is updated.

trusty_uri.description:
The real Trusty URI (an `RA…` artifact code) minted by nanopub-java when this nanopublication is actually published. NOT computed by schema/identity — see schema/trusty-identifiers.md, which is explicit that `RA` must not be reimplemented or approximated.
Distinct from `id`, which is this repository's own `dapper:Nanopublication.{digest}` content address. Two identifiers, two different guarantees: keep them separate and never conflate them.

was_created_at.description: The service that minted this nanopub, e.g. https://nanodash.knowledgepixels.com/.

PackageProvenancedResource.description: The shared attribution + funding + publication + provenance + license + access + mirror slots carried by any citable resource. Applied as a mixin to both `Dataset` (a set of data) and `Set` (a collection of members, e.g. a gene set), so the mirroring invariant and the DataCite/PROV attribution model bind identically to datasets and gene sets. Every `dapper:mirror_mutable: false` slot here is authoritative NIH provenance a mirror MUST NOT rewrite.

PackageSet.description: A collection of members — "an entity that provides a structure to some constituents, which are themselves entities" (prov:Collection). Set is deliberately separate from Dataset: a Dataset is a set of *data* (schema:Dataset); a Set is a set of *things* (genes, proteins, variants). Members are referenced via `prov:hadMember`. Set carries the same attribution/provenance/mirror slots (ProvenancedResource) as Dataset, so a returned set is citable and its authoritative provenance is mirror-protected identically.

ReferenceArchive.description: Outdated-reference stamp on work built on a superseded reference generation. The work keeps every record and stays readable, downloadable and publishable, and paragraph jobs still run; re-analysis and review retry are blocked; start a new analysis on the same gap with current factors instead. reference holds the original anchors. ArchivedReferenceFactor.description: Immutable snapshot of an EAGGL factor referenced by archived work, kept after its reference generation is purged. Public reference data. metadata is the source factor metadata; top_genes (by loading) and top_gene_sets (by rank) hold at most 50 entries each. Legacy cfde-inc-v2 snapshots have a null kpn_trait_id and null gene-set loadings. mechanism.id is the DAPPER Mechanism the catalog served, or null when it could not be minted.

x-contract-rules.schema_validation: Closed DAPPER schemas plus runtime digest, graph-reference, evidence-lineage and citation-span checks.
x-contract-rules.naming: jobs is the only job resource. kind=analysis and kind=paragraph share creation, listing, status, events and cancellation.
x-contract-rules.initial_anchor_retrieval: Existing EAGGL label embeddings joined to a completed exact_trait_factor_number CFDE mapping run; pin routing provenance with each saved request. No label/gene agreement or full-catalog re-embedding prerequisite.
x-contract-rules.reference_generations: Each deployment serves one active EAGGL/CFDE reference generation (model cfde-inc-v2 or eaggl-capped-v1). Work built on a superseded generation carries archive: it stays readable, downloadable and publishable but cannot be re-analysed. See ../docs/reference-reload.md.
x-contract-rules.wire_identity: Compact dapper:Class.digest IDs; absolute external entity URIs. Source aliases remain opaque and exact.
